# Best 18650 chargers

**My pick for most people: XTAR VC4SL (about $32.90)**

- It has four independent bays, USB-C with QC3.0 input, and adjustable current from 0.25A to 3A.
- The LCD shows voltage, current, capacity and internal resistance per cell, and it has capacity-grading and storage modes.
- It fits cells from 10440 to 32650, including protected 21700s, and also charges NiMH.
- Caveats: it defaults to the highest current, so drop it to 500mA-1A with the Curr button for longer cell life. Some reviewers saw it end NiMH charges early or mistake NiMH for Li-ion. It also doesn't list LiFePO4 support.
- [Review and price](https://us.best-batteries.com/reviews/xtar-vc4sl/) (rated 4.3/5). Other reviews: [1Lumen](https://1lumen.com/battery-charger-review/xtar-vc4sl/) and [Stephen Knight](https://www.stephenknightphotography.com/post/charger-review-xtar-vc4sl).

**Runner-up, or if you use LiFePO4: Nitecore UMS4 (about $38.95)**

- It has four independently controlled slots, up to 3A in a single slot (4A total), and a QC input.
- It supports LiFePO4 and Li-ion restoration, and shows internal resistance.
- It has reverse-polarity and short-circuit protection, an overtime timer, and fire-retardant housing.
- [Nitecore product page](https://www.nitecore.com/mobile-product/ums4) and [price/review](https://us.best-batteries.com/reviews/xtar-vc4sl/) (the alternatives list at the bottom).

**Budget simple option: Tenergy TN270 ($18.99)**

- It has two bays and charges at 500mA and 4.2V, so a 3,000mAh cell takes about 6-7 hours.
- It has no USB input and only basic protection (reverse-polarity detection, LED status).
- [Buy at Tenergy via Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/go/tenergy-tn270-li-ion-18650-charger) (affiliate link).

**Other option:** [Smashing Robotics](https://www.smashingrobotics.com/best-18650-battery-chargers/) picked the Keenstone 4-Bay Universal as its top choice (4.6 stars across 4,608 reviews, per that site). I couldn't verify a direct purchase link or independent test data for it. That page is an affiliate listicle, so treat its claims with some caution.

**Tips**
- Avoid unbranded chargers that don't say how they decide a cell is full, and chargers that pair their slots ([VoltRated](https://voltrated.com/guides/best-chargers)).
- Charge at roughly 0.5C-1C when you can. Faster charging is harder on cell life.
- I couldn't check live retailer stock, so confirm the price and that you're buying from an authorized seller.
